title: One row per key, chosen deliberately
why: DISTINCT removes duplicate rows; it cannot pick which row survives. When you need the latest order per customer or the dearest item per order, the shape is ROW_NUMBER() over a partition, filtered to 1. Drill it until you stop reaching for a GROUP BY that cannot carry the other columns along.

variations.prompt: For each customer who has ordered, give the order_id of their most recent order by ordered_at: customer_id and order_id, ordered by customer_id ascending. Break ties on the larger order_id.
variations.reference: SELECT customer_id, order_id FROM (SELECT o.customer_id, o.order_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.customer_id ORDER BY o.ordered_at DESC, o.order_id DESC) AS rn FROM orders o) ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY customer_id

variations.prompt: For each order, give the order_item_id of its dearest line by unit_price: order_id and order_item_id, ordered by order_id ascending. Break ties on the smaller order_item_id.
variations.reference: SELECT order_id, order_item_id FROM (SELECT i.order_id, i.order_item_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY i.order_id ORDER BY i.unit_price DESC, i.order_item_id ASC) AS rn FROM order_items i) ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY order_id

variations.prompt: For each order with at least one payment, give the payment_id of its earliest payment by paid_at, treating a NULL paid_at as later than any timestamp: order_id and payment_id, ordered by order_id ascending. Break ties on the smaller payment_id.
variations.reference: SELECT order_id, payment_id FROM (SELECT p.order_id, p.payment_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.order_id ORDER BY p.paid_at ASC NULLS LAST, p.payment_id ASC) AS rn FROM payments p) ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY order_id
